{{< include _construct_template.qmd >}}

## Construct-specific checks

**Measurement limit: a single item.** Personal relative deprivation is measured with one question ("How would you rate your own financial situation compared to other Germans?"). Internal consistency cannot be estimated. The raw item runs from 1 = much worse to 7 = much better off; the pipeline reverses it so that higher values mean *more* deprivation.

**Convergent validity.** If the item and its reversal are correct, deprivation should correlate negatively with household income.

```{r dep-income}
kable_out(do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(w) {
  dw <- d[d$wave == w, ]
  ok <- !is.na(dw$rel_deprivation) & !is.na(income_num(dw$income))
  data.frame(Wave = w, n = sum(ok),
             `Spearman rho with income` = r2(cor(dw$rel_deprivation[ok],
                                                 income_num(dw$income)[ok], method = "spearman")),
             check.names = FALSE)
})))
```

**Test-retest stability** across waves serves as the reliability evidence for a single item (see the rank-order stability table above).

**Not included:** `deprivation_offender` asks how the government treats offenders compared with the general population. It is a different construct and is not part of this score.
